description: An information-discovery profile for Crohn's disease. It surfaces public trials, publication metadata and carefully filtered headlines; it does not diagnose, recommend treatment or studies, assess eligibility, or interpret findings.

synopsis.overview: Crohn's disease is a chronic inflammatory disease that can affect anywhere from the mouth to the anus. It is one of the main forms of inflammatory bowel disease, but it is distinct from ulcerative colitis and irritable bowel syndrome.
synopsis.manifestations: Symptoms vary with the location and severity of inflammation and may include diarrhoea, abdominal cramping or pain, weight loss, tiredness, fever, anaemia, nausea, joint symptoms, eye inflammation, and skin changes. Periods of active symptoms can alternate with remission, and complications may include strictures, fistulas, abscesses or nutritional problems.
synopsis.management: There is no single treatment plan for everyone. Clinicians may use medicines to reduce inflammation and maintain remission, nutrition and supportive care, monitoring, and surgery for selected complications or disease that does not respond adequately to medicines. Diagnosis and treatment decisions require an appropriately qualified healthcare team.
synopsis.outlook: Crohn's disease varies widely between people and over time. Some people have long periods of remission, while others experience recurring inflammation or complications. Ongoing follow-up helps care teams monitor disease activity, treatment response and nutrition, but a general information profile cannot predict an individual's course.

topics.heading: Clinical trials
topics.description: Registered Crohn's disease studies, including recruitment, study progress and reported results. A listing does not indicate eligibility or that a study is recommended.

topics.heading: Treatment and care
topics.description: Medicines, surgery and multidisciplinary care used to control Crohn's inflammation, manage complications and support remission; treatment choices require clinical assessment.

termDefinitions.budesonide: A corticosteroid medicine used in some inflammatory bowel disease treatment plans; its use and formulation depend on the clinical situation.
termDefinitions.infliximab: A biologic medicine that blocks tumour necrosis factor and may be used for selected inflammatory conditions, including Crohn's disease.
termDefinitions.adalimumab: A biologic medicine that blocks tumour necrosis factor and may be used for selected inflammatory conditions, including Crohn's disease.
termDefinitions.ustekinumab: A biologic medicine that targets interleukin pathways and may be used for selected inflammatory conditions, including Crohn's disease.
termDefinitions.risankizumab: A biologic medicine that targets an interleukin pathway and may be used for selected inflammatory conditions, including Crohn's disease.
termDefinitions.upadacitinib: A small-molecule medicine that affects immune signalling and may be used for selected inflammatory conditions; treatment decisions require clinical assessment.
termDefinitions.biologic therapy: Treatment made using biological molecules, often designed to act on specific immune or inflammatory pathways.

topics.heading: Research
topics.description: Research into Crohn's disease inflammation, immune pathways, genetics, microbiome, biomarkers, treatment response, complications and quality of life.

topics.heading: Genetics and mechanisms
topics.description: Genetic, immune and microbiome research relevant to Crohn's disease, including inherited susceptibility and inflammatory pathways; genetic findings require qualified interpretation.

termDefinitions.NOD2: A gene involved in recognising components of microbes and regulating immune responses; variants are associated with susceptibility to some Crohn's disease patterns.
termDefinitions.IL23R: A gene encoding part of an interleukin-23 receptor; variation in this pathway has been studied in inflammatory bowel disease susceptibility.
termDefinitions.TNF: A signalling protein involved in inflammation. Tumour-necrosis-factor inhibitors are one class of medicines used in some inflammatory diseases.
termDefinitions.genetic susceptibility: An inherited tendency that may alter risk; it does not by itself establish that someone will develop Crohn's disease.

topics.heading: Living with Crohn's disease
topics.description: Daily life with Crohn's disease, including fluctuating symptoms, fatigue, nutrition, work, school, relationships, mental wellbeing and planning around care.

topics.heading: Caregiving and support
topics.description: Family and care-partner support, practical help, communication, care coordination, education and services for people affected by Crohn's disease.

topics.heading: Advocacy and access
topics.description: Crohn's disease awareness, patient voice, access to diagnosis and specialist care, disability inclusion, policy, research funding and public advocacy.
